name: Grid connection and interconnection studies
principle: A connection must satisfy the Malaysian Grid Code, which the Grid System Operator owns and administers. The chain is load-flow, short-circuit and transient-stability modelling of the proposed connection, then compliance checks for voltage limits, fault ride-through and reactive capability, then a connection agreement with TNB and GSO approval before energisation. Industrial loads above about 25,000 kVA take supply at 132 kV or 275 kV, which places them inside grid-code territory.

performance.basis: TNB supplies 132 kV and 275 kV for demands above about 25,000 kVA
TNB limits at 132 kV and 275 kV

gaps.item: study cost per MW connected, with a Malaysian consultant benchmark
gaps.reason: No published study fee exists: regulators publish deposits and milestone payments, not consultant fees. The MISO M2 milestone ($8,000/MW, 2024) is recorded as adjacent data with that caveat. Commercial study fees are quoted privately; searched 2026-11-16.

where.hint: Ask the owner for a benchmarked study cost

gaps.action: Leave open until a source states this exact metric and scope.

costs.basis: MISO raised its M2 milestone payment from $4,000/MW to $8,000/MW at the queue application deadline. This is a refundable-at-risk DEPOSIT tied to capacity, not the cost of performing a connection study - recorded because no study fee is published anywhere.

source.note: US DOE, MISO interconnection queue reform policy note (Aug 2024), M2 milestone on p.15, read 2026-11-16
